facts.text: The tree martin averages 13 cm long and has a shallowly forked tail.
facts.quote: The tree martin averages 13 cm (5.1 in) in length and has a shallowly forked tail.

facts.text: It has an iridescent blue back and crown, a rufous forehead and a whitish rump.
facts.quote: The adult has an iridescent blue back and crown, brown wings and tail, a rufous forehead and a whitish rump.

facts.text: Its call is a tsweet and its song is a high-pitched twitter.
facts.quote: The call of this vocal swallow is a tsweet and the song is a high-pitched twitter.

facts.text: Nests go in natural holes in dead trees or rock crevices, but increasingly on bridges and buildings.
facts.quote: Nests are constructed in natural holes in dead trees or rock crevices, but increasingly in artificial sites on bridges and buildings.

facts.text: It occasionally relines the nests of welcome swallows and may displace the owners to take the nest.
facts.quote: Tree martins also occasionally reline the nests of welcome swallows, and may displace the owners to obtain the nest.

facts.text: The clutch is usually four brown and mauve-spotted white eggs, and the species is often double-brooded.
facts.quote: The clutch is 3–5, usually four, brown and mauve-spotted white eggs, and this species is often double-brooded.

facts.text: It breeds mostly south of latitude 20°S in Australia and on Timor island.
facts.quote: It breeds in Australia, mostly south of latitude 20°S, and on Timor island.

facts.text: It winters through most of Australia, New Guinea, Indonesia east of the Wallace Line, and the Solomon Islands.
facts.quote: It is migratory, wintering through most of Australia, New Guinea, Indonesia east of the Wallace Line, and the Solomon Islands.

facts.text: It is increasingly common in urban and suburban areas and prefers open woodland with large trees for nest holes.
facts.quote: This is a bird of open woodland, preferably with large trees to provide nest holes. It is increasingly common in urban and suburban areas.
